title: 'We Never Stopped Believing': Raichandani on India's Last-Ball U19 Asia Cup Final Win
excerpt: India's U19 captain, who made 80 in the chase of 338, said the plan was always to take the final deep - and that the dressing room trusted a batting order that ran almost 11 deep.
body:
• India U19 captain Lakshya Raichandani said the plan in Saturday's Asia Cup final was to take the chase of 338 deep, speaking to ANI as the team arrived in New Delhi on Sunday.
  • India had collapsed to 252 for eight before Manal Chauhan and Mohit Ulva turned the final; Ulva's unbeaten 49 finished the chase off the last ball.
  • Raichandani defended the team's celebrations: "A lot of emotions come out when you win a match like this."
  • The win gave India a record ninth U19 Asia Cup title, their first since 2021.

A day after captaining India to a one-wicket, last-ball win over Pakistan in the U19 Asia Cup final, Lakshya Raichandani said the chase was built on a simple plan and a dressing room that refused to give it up. Speaking to ANI after arriving at Indira Gandhi International Airport in New Delhi on Sunday, the India U19 captain described how the team held its nerve after slipping to 252 for eight chasing 338 at Al Amerat in Oman.

"Everyone in the dressing room had complete belief in each other. We were playing with almost 11 batters, so we never stopped believing, and we were quite optimistic, and thankfully we chased it."

- Lakshya Raichandani, India U19 captain, speaking to ANI

"Our plan was simply to take the game deep"

"Nothing, our plan was simply to take the game deep, and hopefully we took the game deep, and we knew the wicket was good so the chase would be easy," Raichandani told ANI. "The atmosphere was quite tense in the dressing room, but we had belief, we were quite optimistic, so it was quite good." The depth he pointed to was real: India's batting ran so deep that the last two wickets produced the winning runs, with No. 10 Mohit Ulva unbeaten on 49.

How the final swung

Pakistan, who batted first, made 337 for nine on Usman Khan's 107, Abdul Qadir's 80 and captain Farhan Yousaf's 63. Raichandani and Aaryavir Sehwag opened India's reply with a 95-run stand - the captain made 80 off 101 balls and Sehwag 58 off 61 - before the chase collapsed to 252 for eight. Manal Chauhan's 47 off 32 balls revived it, and after his dismissal Ulva took India home with Chigurupati Venkata (11 not out) at the other end, finishing the match off the final delivery. Our full report of the final reconstructs the last overs ball by ball. Ulva was named player of the match; Sehwag, the tournament's leading run-scorer with 361 runs, was player of the tournament.

The celebrations, defended

Raichandani was also asked about the Indian players' celebrations after the winning boundary, and made no apology for them. "It was completely justified. A lot of emotions come out when you win a match like this - it's a final match, so you know how hard you've worked to win the match, so those emotions just came out," he said. The title is India's ninth in the U19 Asia Cup, a record, and their first since 2021; it also avenged the 2025 final, in which Pakistan beat India by 191 runs to take the trophy India have now won back.
